newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Troops kill over 40 rebels in Algeria - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Troops kill over 40 rebels in Algeria - newspaper.

text.p: Algerian troops have killed more than 40 rebels and are besieging more than 200 guerrillas in a huge assault on the headquarters of the main Moslem rebel leader in western Algeria, an Algerian newspaper said on Monday.

Troops helped by paramilitary forces have fanned out in a major operation in El Gouassem town in the western province of Tissemsilt since last Wednesday, where they killed more than 40 rebels and are besieging more than 200, said El Watan, quoting security sources and residents.
They were ringing the headquarters of Ahmed Benaicha, deputy chief of the Islamic Salvation Army (AIS), the armed wing of the outlawed radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), the paper said.
The rebel headquarters was used a training ground for the Moslem guerrillas and contained a rebel field hospital, it said.
The government troops' advance was slow because of the rugged area and mines planted by the rebels, it added.

Two similar anti-guerrilla operations were going on near the western Maghnia region near the Moroccan border, and near Khemis el Khechna, some 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, said El Watan, widely seen as well-informed on security matters.
The authorities have made no statement so far on the reported operations, midway through campaigning for the June 5 parliamentary election.

The government, fighting a five-year-old campaign by Moslem militants, has offered residents 4.5 million dinars (over $80,000) for information leading to the capture or killing of Benaicha and AIS's chief, Madani Merzag, as well their most feared rival Armed Islamic Group (GIA) commander Antar Zouabri.
Benaicha's besieged guerrillas were armed with "several" Kalashnikov assault rifles and a huge amount of ammunition, El Watan reported.
Security forces said on Saturday they had shot dead four Moslem rebel leaders along with 13 fellow guerrillas thanks to citizens' tipoffs in return for substantial government rewards.

About 60,000 people have been killed in violence pitting Moslem rebels against government forces since 1992, when authorities cancelled a general election in which the radical FIS had taken a huge lead.
"Peace" has topped the agendas of the more than 7,000 candidates battling to win over apathetic voters in the current campaign.
